name: Narrative Fidelity Audit Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for the quality of a fidelity audit run over a fact-based narrative. Scores the AUDIT, not the draft. An audit that reports a clean draft without evidence of having run the expensive passes scores low regardless of how tidy its output looks.

criteria.name: Bright-Line Coverage and Disposition
criteria.description: Whether all fourteen bright lines were swept, breaches recorded with line references, and each breach given one of the four dispositions (DELETE, DOWNGRADE, DECLARE, RESEARCH) rather than being drafted-and-flagged

scores.1: No systematic sweep; breaches noted impressionistically or not at all
scores.2: Some lines swept; breaches listed without line references or dispositions
scores.3: All lines swept; most breaches have a disposition, but some are left as 'flag for review'
scores.4: All lines swept, breaches referenced to specific text, every breach dispositioned, no fifth disposition used
scores.5: All lines swept with per-line counts; every breach dispositioned with the replacement text or the specific research request written out

criteria.name: Interiority Provenance Rigor
criteria.description: Whether every interior-state and intentionality claim (person and system) was tagged [A]/[B]/[C]/[D], the [D] count reported as a number, and the zero-D gate enforced

scores.1: Interior states not tagged; 'he realized', 'the market decided' pass unchallenged
scores.2: Person interiority tagged; system intentionality verbs missed entirely
scores.3: Both tagged, [D] count reported, but some [D] items left in the draft with a caveat instead of removed
scores.4: Both tagged, [D] count reported as a number, gate enforced, each [D] converted to observable behaviour or attributed speech
scores.5: As 4, plus every [B] artefact carries its written alternative reading, and substitutes for unfillable realization beats were chosen and stress-tested by striking untraceable nouns and verbs

criteria.name: Over-Correction Control
criteria.description: Whether the audit checked in the other direction: that [A] and [B] material is NOT hedged, that hedge load was measured, and that hedge saturation was diagnosed as under-reporting rather than fixed by deleting attributions

scores.1: No over-correction check; sourced thought left hedged, or attributions added indiscriminately
scores.2: Notices hedging in passing but offers no measurement and no diagnosis
scores.3: Hedge load measured; some sourced-but-hedged sentences flagged
scores.4: Hedge load measured against a stated budget, all sourced-but-hedged sentences flagged and unhedged, diagnosis of saturation is under-reporting
scores.5: As 4, plus red-flag deletions are reported alongside sourced-and-kept counts, demonstrating the scan keyed on missing pointers rather than on vividness

criteria.name: Multi-Altitude Verification
criteria.description: Whether the How-Do-You-Know pass ran at paragraph and passage level, not only at sentence level, and whether the absence of higher-altitude defects was treated as evidence the pass did not run

scores.1: Sentence-level checking only; reports a clean piece
scores.2: Paragraph questions nominally asked but produce no findings and no comment on that fact
scores.3: Defects found at sentence and paragraph level; passage level thin or skipped
scores.4: Defects reported separately at all three altitudes, including implicature, ordering-as-causation, and fairness-to-subject findings
scores.5: As 4, plus the audit explicitly states that zero higher-altitude defects would mean the pass did not run, and reports counts per altitude to prove it did

criteria.name: Subtraction and Proportion
criteria.description: Whether the subtraction log was assembled and reviewed AS A SET, the omission check listed corpus items absent from the draft, and proportion asymmetries were given written justifications rather than mechanical rebalancing

scores.1: No subtraction log, no omission check; only additions were policed
scores.2: Cuts reviewed individually; each found defensible; no set-level question asked
scores.3: Log assembled and reviewed as a set, but no omission check or no proportion table
scores.4: Set review asks whether cuts share a direction, omission check lists absent corpus items with reasons, proportion asymmetries flagged
scores.5: As 4, plus written justifications required for each asymmetry, causal weights recorded independently of the arc, and the absence of a log reported as a RETURN TO RESEARCH finding

criteria.name: Provenance Integrity
criteria.description: Whether pointers were resolved mechanically, circular citations into the pipeline's own outputs caught, sources annotated with interest as well as date, and secondary retrospectives barred from carrying documented-mechanism causal tags

scores.1: Pointers accepted on sight; no resolution attempted
scores.2: Pointers checked by reading; granularity not enforced ('the 10-K' accepted)
scores.3: Pointers resolved and granularity enforced; circular-citation check not run mechanically
scores.4: Mechanical circular-citation check run and reported; pointer granularity enforced throughout
scores.5: As 4, plus per-source interest annotation and primary/secondary tagging, with any G1 mechanism tag sourced from a retrospective downgraded

criteria.name: Disclosure Discipline
criteria.description: Whether the note on sources was generated from the deviation log after drafting, boilerplate refused, empty registers stated affirmatively, in-body placement enforced within two sentences of the claim, and the inversion check run

scores.1: Boilerplate disclaimer emitted, or no note produced
scores.2: Note produced but written as prose in advance of the deviation log; generic category language
scores.3: Note generated from the log; placement rules not enforced or inversion check skipped
scores.4: Generated from the log, empty registers stated affirmatively, in-body placement enforced, inversion check run and reported
scores.5: As 4, plus disclosures marked non-removable, hedge/disclosure budget reported, and over-budget treated as a signal to change architecture rather than add caveats

criteria.name: Vocabulary and Verdict Honesty
criteria.description: Whether the audit consistently says 'sourced' rather than 'verified', emits the full gate verdict block with no omitted fields, and surfaces rather than resolves questions about named parties in adversarial roles

scores.1: Claims the draft was 'fact-checked' or 'verified'; no verdict block
scores.2: Verdict given informally; verification language appears at least once
scores.3: Correct vocabulary; verdict block present but with fields omitted
scores.4: Correct vocabulary throughout, full verdict block, CLEARED AS SOURCED used as the strongest available verdict
scores.5: As 4, plus named parties in adversarial roles and right-of-reply gaps surfaced for human decision rather than quietly softened in the prose

passing_note: Average score must be >= 3.5 for the audit to count as run. A score below 3 in 'Multi-Altitude Verification' or 'Subtraction and Proportion' invalidates the audit outright regardless of the average: those are the two passes that catch the fully-sourced-but-false piece, and an audit missing them is more dangerous than no audit, because its output reads as checked.
